[openai] Finding 1 (edge-case, medium): AC1's "first parseable timestamp" must validate the timestamp is actually parseable, not just present, before treating it as the session start. Recommend guarding with a real parse check (e.g. !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(...))), tested with an invalid-then-valid timestamp pair.

Finding 2 (dependency, medium): AC2's test must prove the FULL path (resolver scenario -> artifact rail), not just the footer-scanner unit in isolation, since readTranscriptTail's own clamp is an equally necessary part of the fix. Add a resolver/route-level regression test alongside the run-id-recovery.ts unit test.

Finding 3 (approach, low): Don't duplicate the transient-error text-match in both missionActivityFeedResolve.ts and missionActivityFeedReconcile.ts; classify once at the tool-result boundary.

Overall verdict: revise. All three findings should be folded into the mini-plan before build.
plan.contradiction_resolution: Only one reviewer (openai/codex) responded; glm errored locally (openai python package not installed on this machine, unrelated to the change). Per external_review.py's own degraded-mode contract, one opinion is enough to proceed. All 3 openai findings were triaged as fix and folded into the spec/mini-plan before build.

findings.finding: Splicing a transient-rejected test card out of cards/testCards/awaitingTestResult in missionActivityFeedResolve.ts left it still reachable as a value in the pre-existing state.authoringConsumedBy map whenever the dropped card was also a TDD authoring run. A later, out-of-order rollback of its backing Write (rollbackFailedWrite/unstampAuthoringRun in missionActivityFeedAuthoringRollback.ts) could look the detached card up and misread its "neither failed nor pending" shape as a SUCCESSFUL recovery, wrongly clearing an unrelated, still-open genuine test failure's red status.
findings.suggestion: Purge the matching authoringConsumedBy entry (and clear card.authoringRun) at splice time, so a later rollback behaves as if this run had never consumed the tracker slot.

findings.finding: The AC3/AC4 work pushed missionActivityFeedResolve.ts from its already-at-ceiling 300 lines to 332+, violating the project's file-size convention.
findings.suggestion: Split into cohesive files (the splice+purge helper, and the pre-existing untouched generic blocker branch) rather than trimming comments.

code.disposition: both findings (high authoringConsumedBy dangling-ref, medium bloat) fixed before commit; see mini-plan step 6

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Purging state.authoringConsumedBy at drop time (the code-review fix) is sufficient to prevent a spliced transient-rejected card from being resurrected by a later out-of-order Write rollback. — authoringConsumedBy is not the only path into unstampAuthoringRun — state.restoreValidationPending is a second, deferred one, populated when a same-turn SECOND Write/Edit to the same path fails while its own EARLIER write's fate is still unknown (missionActivityFeedAuthoringRollback.ts's else branch, keyed by the earlier write's tool_use id rather than the later one authoringConsumedBy uses). A card can remain a value there even after its authoringConsumedBy entry was already purged, since the two maps are keyed by different tool_use ids belonging to different writes. Reproduced with a three-tool_use fixture (w0, w1 both targeting the same path, then an authoring run) with results delivered in the order w1-error, authoring-transient-reject, w0-error: without a second purge of restoreValidationPending, the dropped card's command wrongly resurfaces merged into an unrelated genuine npm test failure.

doubt.disposition: restoreValidationPending second-path finding fixed before commit, verified via revert-run-restore regression test

findings.finding: The spec's Test Completeness Ledger for AC4 claims a test proving "a legitimate recovered failure-then-pass card is NOT wrongly dropped (the regression the reconcile-filter approach broke)." The shown test file contains no such case — it has the transient-drop test, the genuine-failure negative control, and the two authoring-resurrection probes, but no fixture where a test invocation genuinely fails and then genuinely recovers on retry. The closest test (transient-reject → real retry passes) does not exercise the merged recovery-card shape that motivated reverting the reconcile-filter approach.
findings.suggestion: Add a fixture: `npm test` fails (is_error), then a retry succeeds, asserting the merged/recovered card survives with a resolved pill. Without it, a regression reintroducing over-aggressive dropping of wordless recovered cards would pass this suite.

findings.finding: For a non-test bucket (e.g. a subrunner `Agent` dispatch) rejected by the transient classifier, the result is skipped entirely — the pending card stays `running` forever once the run ends, which is the same "stuck Running… / unclickable" symptom AC6 fixes, just via a different trigger. The spec only requires the blocker case, so this is consistent with AC3's letter, but it leaves a reachable stuck state.
findings.suggestion: Consider demoting a transient-rejected subrunner card (or dropping it) the way the test bucket is handled; at minimum document the known gap.

findings.finding: The comment says "a leading partial line was dropped whenever the read did not start at byte 0" — if the positional-read primitive (`readChunk`) already strips the byte-cut partial line before returning `r.chunk.content`, then `findRunIdFooter` dropping its first line again on `startedMidFile` discards one additional complete line per wide read, which could be the very line carrying the `Run-ID:` footer at the window boundary. The route-level test can't distinguish this because the harness returns raw text with no stripping.
findings.suggestion: Confirm readChunk does not strip partial lines (if it doesn't, this is moot); if it does, drop the scanner-side line-drop when the reader reports it already stripped, or key the flag off "fragment still present."  Spec compliance check (no defect): AC1–AC6 are each visibly implemented and pinned by tests that exercise the reported shape (real transcript-measured texts, byte-cut fragments, `Agent` dispatch, `queued_command` attachment); AC7 is verification-only as specified. The `note` kind is fully wired (`ActivityKind`, icon map, accent map, E2E assertion updated). The `startedMidFile` threading is additive with default `false`, so unshown callers compile and behave unchanged. No security concerns — the new attachment bridge validates shape and returns `null` on anything unrecognized, and the recovery scan stays bounded.  Overall assessment: Ship-with-fixes — the implementation matches the spec and the review cascade caught genuinely deep state bugs, but the AC4 "legitimate recovery kept" test claimed in the ledger is missing from the shipped test file and should be added, and the two low edge cases deserve a confirmation or a documented gap.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: The early `continue` for a transient error in a non-test bucket skips `rollbackFailedWrite`. If auto mode rejects a `Write` or `Edit` of a test file, its tracker remains even though the write never ran; a later test command can then be misclassified as an authoring run.
findings.suggestion: Run the existing write rollback for transiently rejected writes before skipping card resolution.

findings.finding: startedMidFile` always drops the first line. A bounded read can start after byte 0 exactly at a JSONL line boundary; if that complete first line contains the only footer, recovery loses it.
findings.suggestion: Have the reader report whether the first line is actually partial, or inspect the byte preceding the read offset before dropping it.

findings.finding: The route tests inject a short transcript through the harness and assert only `scenario` and `runId`. They would pass with the old 1 MiB reader cap and do not check the artifact rail or AC7’s Review and Decisions chips. The main reported failure is therefore not protected by these tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a test using the real bounded reader with a footer beyond 1 MiB, then assert the required artifacts in the response.  The change addresses the reported paths, but these cases need fixes before shipping. Ship with fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

external_code.disposition: openai finding 1 (rollbackFailedWrite skip) fixed; deeper root cause found during triage of openai finding 1's sibling (glm subrunner stuck-card finding): generic is_error branch pre-empted the subrunner bucket entirely, fixed by reordering; openai finding 2/glm finding 3 (startedMidFile double-drop) rejected with reason (readTailFromDisk is a raw byte read, no boundary snap, so dropping the leading line is the correct conservative default); glm finding 1/openai finding 3 (test rigor) addressed: genuine fail-then-retry coverage already exists pre-iterate (missionActivityFeed.test.ts), and wire.ts's own fromByte/startedMidFile arithmetic (previously untested at any level) now has direct coverage in the new wire.test.ts
